venture.ventureIdea: CampusEase is a student-focused convenience platform that helps college students access everyday essentials and services within or near campus. Students can order stationery, snacks, medicines, personal-care products and other urgent essentials through a mobile/web platform and receive them at convenient campus pickup points or hostels. The platform can partner with nearby retailers and campus vendors, creating a hyperlocal delivery ecosystem. What makes CampusEase different is its focus on student-specific needs, affordable pricing, quick delivery and convenient campus-based fulfillment.

mission0.initialCustomer: College and university students, particularly hostel students and students living away from home. The initial target segment would be students aged 18–25 who frequently need snacks, stationery, personal-care products, medicines and other daily essentials.
mission0.geography: Doon University and nearby college/student clusters in Dehradun, Uttarakhand.
mission0.whyChosen: I chose this idea because students frequently face convenience and accessibility problems in getting everyday essentials. My exposure to marketing and logistics helped me identify an opportunity to combine customer needs, local retail partnerships and efficient delivery into a student-focused solution.

frictions.friction: Students often need everyday essentials urgently but nearby stores may be inconvenient to reach, especially when they are busy with classes or staying in hostels.
frictions.evidenceSource: Personal observation and informal discussions with college students about their everyday shopping difficulties.
frictions.currentWorkaround: Students walk to nearby shops, ask friends to bring items, order from general delivery apps, or wait until they can visit a store.
frictions.whenOccurs: During busy class schedules, late evenings, exam periods, and when students suddenly need essential items.
frictions.whyWorkaroundUnsatisfactory: It can take time, involve extra delivery charges, depend on friends' availability, and may not provide quick access to campus-specific needs.
frictions.whoExperiences: College and university students, especially hostel students and students living away from home.

mission1.confidenceEvidenceNeeded: Surveying 50–100 students about their frequency of urgent purchases, time spent accessing nearby stores, delivery charges paid, and products they most frequently need.

conservative.notes: Low initial adoption among DGU hostel students due to limited awareness and cautious student spending. Growth depends mainly on word-of-mouth and repeat users.

base.notes: Steady adoption through campus promotion, student referrals and partnerships with nearby retailers. Students use the service regularly for urgent everyday essentials.

ambitious.notes: High adoption supported by official campus promotion, multiple nearby retail partners, reliable delivery and strong repeat usage across DGU hostels.

mission8.totalCustomersEvidence: Estimated total DGU student population representing the broad potential customer universe.
mission8.annualSpendEvidence: Based on ₹30 delivery/service fee × 2 purchases per month × 12 months.
mission8.serviceableEvidence: Estimated DGU hostel students aged 18–25 who regularly need everyday essentials and can be served through campus delivery.
mission8.obtainableEvidence: 12-month target based on a realistic initial capture of approximately 20% of the serviceable hostel-student segment through campus promotion, referrals and retailer partnerships.
mission8.mostUrgentAssumption: We need to validate whether at least 25% of our target students are willing to use CampusEase and pay for the service, allowing us to realistically acquire up to 300 customers within the first year

mission12.reflectionNotes: CampusEase aims to solve a common student problem by making access to campus services more convenient and time-saving. Through this venture plan, I identified the importance of validating willingness to pay, repeat usage and customer acquisition. The next step is to test the MVP with real students, collect feedback and improve the solution based on actual user behaviour.
